text: M17 ce8plh8i names two causes of `shadow-only`: a conflicting trial merge and a git older than 2.38 (mergeTree 'unsupported'). M28 eu1rffp6 also lets mergeTree answer `{ status: 'error' }` (any other failure of `git merge-tree` on a supported git). The specification does not say what the shadow diff answers then, and the endpoint's refusals (VALIDATION, GIT_UNAVAILABLE, SHADOW_NOT_FOUND) do not cover it. Assumed: a failed trial merge (and a failed file list / commit list under a detected repository) is a server fault — 500 with the shared error envelope — not a silent fall to `shadow-only`, which would present a broken merge as a conflict-free 'what the shadow did'.
assumption: ASSUMPTION:dev-4601 — a trial merge that fails on a supported git is a server fault (500), not a fall to shadow-only.
